• Subscriber-only quarterly events at the press itself
Creative.mission: To restore the printed press sheet as a primary publication object, set on a working letterpress.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Press Sheet is the printer's trade name for a single sheet pulled from the printing press — the foundational unit of letterpress and offset printing. Creative.manifesto: Most modern newsletters ship in email and print as an afterthought. We started The Press Sheet Co to invert the order. Every issue is set on our working letterpress, printed onto a single broadsheet sheet, and posted to subscribers. The email arrives two weeks later as a transcription, not the primary publication. The press is the product.
Creative.industrySummary: Letterpress printing has a small but committed audience and is rarely used as the primary publication medium for a subscription newsletter. There is real space for a creative-led publication that uses letterpress as the primary medium and treats email as the secondary distribution.
Creative.competitorLandscape: The Saturday Paper (thesaturdaypaper.com.au) plays the closest peer in printed weekly publication. The Stinging Fly (stingingfly.org) holds the small-press literary peer slot. McSweeney's Quarterly (mcsweeneys.net) sits in the heritage-design publication peer position. The Marginalian (themarginalian.org) plays the digital-essayist peer reference. We sit further out with letterpress as the primary medium.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Press Sheet Co is a monthly letterpress-printed newsletter posted to subscribers in print, with email distribution as a secondary channel.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the medium. Letterpress is the primary publication; the email is the transcription. The press is the marketing.

targetAudience.primary: Subscribers 30-60 who collect printed publications and care about typography, printing tradition, and physical media.
behaviors: Subscribe to small-press publications.
Visit print shops, type foundries, and binderies.
Display printed broadsheets and posters at home.
Pay full subscription rates for printed media.
motivations: Want a printed broadsheet posted to their door.
Want a publication set on a working press.
Want access to the press as part of the subscription.

dos: Print every issue on the press first.
Photograph the press, the type, and the working room in marketing material.
Reference the typeface and the paper stock on every issue's masthead.
Sign correspondence by the printer-editor.
